metadata.case_name: LEE PING FOON v. LI HOI T/A HOI TAT CONSTRUCTION & DECORATION ENGINEERING

injuries.description: the right eye had no light perception and it was totally blind.
source: the right eye had no light perception and it was totally blind.

injuries.description: the nail head struck his left eye, resulting in a large corneal laceration.
source: the nail head struck his left eye, resulting in a large corneal laceration.
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration without prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

injuries.description: he was then found to have a traumatic cataract so that a third operation for left cataract extraction was performed on 27.2.1995.
source: he was then found to have a traumatic cataract so that a third operation for left cataract extraction was performed on 27.2.1995.

injuries.description: He is now virtually unable to see.
source: He is now virtually unable to see.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of eye or orbit, unspecified

manifestations.description: pain watering and photophobia in the left eye
can barely see and can at best make out a blurred outline of the objects in front of him
Doctor Paul Cheung considered him to have suffered a 95% disability in his left eye

treatments_received: operation to repair the lacerated wound and to reposition and suture back the corneal tissue
second operation on 6.2.1995 for a conjunctival flap
third operation for left cataract extraction on 27.2.1995
follow up treatment at the Eye Hospital
treatments_future: possible future surgery (doctor observed disability of left eye may be reduced to 70% to 80% by a future surgery at the cost of about $65,000)

losses.description: Loss of vision in the left eye leaving him virtually blind (the right eye was already totally blind).
